quote: Problem 6020: Friendly Integers, American Mathematical Monthly, volume 84, pages 65-66
posed_by: Claude W. Anderson and Dean R. Hickerson
note: Anderson and Hickerson formally introduced the concept of solitary numbers and friendly numbers in their 1977 American Mathematical Monthly problem. A solitary number is a positive integer with a unique abundancy index (σ(n)/n, where σ(n) is the sum of divisors). The question of whether 10 is solitary — i.e., whether 10 has a 'friend' with the same abundancy index — was posed as part of this foundational work and remains open.
